4 16-04-2024 Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned counsel for the informant/victim-respondent no.2 and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.
2. Records have been placed before this Court to consider the prayer of the appellant for suspension of his sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal.
3. The appellant in this case has been convicted vide judgment dated 30.01.2023 and order of sentence dated 02.02.2023 by learned ADJ-VII-cum-Special Judge, POCSO, Katihar in connection with G.R. Case No. 2250 of 2020 arising out of Korha P.S. Case No. 263 of 2020 and he has been ordered to undergo rigorous imprisonment for twenty years and to pay a fine Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.299 of 2023(4) dt.16-04-2024 of Rs.50,000/- for the offence under Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and in default of payment of fine, he has to further undergo six months rigorous imprisonment.

sentences.text: As per the prosecution story, the victim-respondent no.2 fell in love with the accused-appellant and he established physical relationship with the victim for several months on false pretext of marriage which resulted into her pregnancy.
It is further alleged that the victim was aged about seventeen years at the time of her pregnancy and the appellant and his family members were not ready to accept her.

5. On the last date of hearing, this Court had taken note of the submissions of learned counsel for the appellants wherein it had been noticed that all the prosecution witnesses including the mother of the victim, the victim herself and her brother have consistently deposed that the victim and the appellant were in love with each other.
The victim had been living in the house of the appellant and she has given birth to a child who is now one year old.
6. This Court found that the learned trial court had recorded a finding as regards the age of the victim based on the testimony of the headmaster of the school who deposed as PW-5.
Patna High Court CR.

According to the said finding, the victim girl was minor, however, it was pointed out to this Court that in his cross-examination, the headmaster (PW-5) has stated that in the school admission register where the date of birth of the victim is stated, there is no signature of either the parents or the guardian of the victim girl and it does not contain photograph of the victim.

7. The appellant made a submission before this Court that the victim girl had made a categorical statement that she and the appellant both are ready to marry and she was not interested in pursuing the matter.
8. Today, Mr. Subodh Kumar Barnwal, learned counsel has entered appearance on behalf of the victim girl who was earlier impleaded as respondent no.2.
Learned counsel for respondent no.2 submits on instruction that he would have no objection to the prayer of the appellant for his suspension of sentence and release on bail.
It is submitted that the victim girl has given birth to a child out of the relationship between the appellant and her and now they want to marry each other in order to live a happy conjugal life.
It is also stated that respondent no.2 is major.

9. In the given circumstance, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State does not oppose the prayer for bail of the appellant, however, it is submitted that for the present, a provisional bail for a period of six months may be granted to the Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.299 of 2023(4)
dt.16-04-2024 appellant to provide him an opportunity to go for a marriage with the victim and then come back to this Court with complete information.

10. Having regard to the submissions noted hereinabove, this Court directs suspension of sentence and release of the appellant during pendency of the appeal on provisional bail for a period of six months from the date of his release on submission of bail bonds of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned ADJ-VII-cum-Special Judge, POCSO, Katihar in connection with G.R. Case No. 2250 of 2020 arising out of Korha P.S. Case No. 263 of 2020.
